[engine] Before analysing whether a setting is missing from a resolved configuration, check the control flow that emits it. A setting can be absent because of an if/else nesting error rather than because a default is off -- and the two are indistinguishable from the resolved output alone, while requiring opposite fixes.

<!-- lesson_id: eng-gate-0013 | class: gate-integrity | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `gate-integrity`

## 為什麼（because）

CGC_LOOP_GUARD was absent from the launch env whenever CGC_SOFT_POOL_L1 was set. That is NOT 'guarded by a default of off': the guard block had been swallowed into the L1 else-branch, so the knob was UNREACHABLE in that configuration, and CGC_LOOP_GUARD=1 could not turn it back on. Evidence: grep for LOOP_GUARD in run_server.sh returns exactly one push site (lines 1388-1390), which is textually inside the L1 else-branch, closed by a doubled `fi`; and the measured 4-input table (default / L0 / L1 / L0+L1) matches the nesting prediction rather than a default-value prediction. Why the distinction is expensive: the wrong reading ('it is just off by default') leads to 'pass the flag' -- which is precisely the action that does not work here. The same day's presence-gated defect is the mirror image: there the value lied while the structure was fine; here the structure lies while the value is ignored.

## 反例（counterexample_observed）

`CGC_SOFT_POOL_L1=48 CGC_LOOP_GUARD=1` -- a user explicitly requesting the guard ON -- produced no CGC_LOOP_GUARD in the env, because the request and the emission live in mutually exclusive branches of the same if. The knob was not defaulted off; it was unreachable.

## 適用於（applies_to）

- `scripts/run_server.sh`
- `agent_harness/CONVENTIONS.md`
